docs.title: Welcome to the DIFFER-PLD4E-schemas documentation
docs.text: A NOMAD plugin with the electronic lab notebook (ELN) schemas of the PLD4Energy lab at DIFFER.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The plugin adds these entry types to NOMAD:

Entry type Use it for SA-PLD Logbook One run on the SA-PLD system: laser calibration, targets, substrates, process steps and in-situ data. LA-PLD Logbook One run on the LA-PLD system. Same as SA-PLD, plus the larger carriers, the particle reduction plate and polar/cartesian heater scans. PLD Target One physical target (the target database). PLD Substrate One substrate/sample (the substrate database). Usually created for you by a logbook. PLD In-situ Techniques In-situ measurements (RHEED, MIC, SE, LA-EDS, OES, SHG) that are not part of a new deposition run, e.g. post-processing of an older sample. Deposition A sputter deposition run (the original sputter schemas of this plugin).

It also adds the PLD logbook dashboard: a guided form for SA-PLD and LA-PLD runs that shows only the fields that apply and only saves complete logbooks. See Use the PLD logbook dashboard.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: This page explains how the PLD schemas are put together and why. It is background for users who want to understand the behaviour, and for maintainers who change the schemas.

docs.title: From the mock-up to NOMAD
docs.text:
The schemas started from the PLD4Energy ELN mock-up (an HTML form) and the users' feedback on it. The mock-up is a form, not a data model, so repeated parts of the form became reusable sections:

In the mock-up In the schema The gas checkboxes and flow fields, repeated in every step One BackgroundGas section, repeated per gas in every step Laser fields, repeated in pre-ablation and deposition One LaserParameters section (laser) "Substrate stage start x/y/z/tilt/spin-position" One HeaterStagePosition section with x, y, z, tilt, spin Target stage fields One TargetStage section Laser details in the system details LaserCalibration (laser_details) Fields shown only for a choice (scan yes/no, polar/cartesian) Optional sub-sections, added on save for the chosen option "Number of targets/substrates" counters Repeating sub-sections: add as many as you need In-situ techniques inside the deposition step A separate in_situ_techniques section and a stand-alone entry type

NOMAD forms cannot show or hide a field depending on another field. Conditional fields are therefore optional sub-sections. The section for the chosen option is added on save, so its fields appear without having to add it by hand.

docs.title: Entries and how they refer to each other
docs.text:
PLD Target (entry)            PLD Substrate (entry)
      ▲                           ▲          ▲
      │ target                    │ substrate│ sample
      │                           │          │
SA-PLD / LA-PLD Logbook (entry)   │    PLD In-situ Techniques (entry)
├── laser_details                 │
├── targets[]  ── target ─────────┼──► PLD Target
├── substrates[] ── substrate ────┘   (created on save)
├── load_recipe ── recipe ──► earlier logbook of the same system
├── steps[]
│   ├── Pre-ablation step ── target ──► PLD Target
│   ├── Heating step
│   ├── Pulsed laser deposition step ── target, substrate
│   └── Cool-down step
└── in_situ_techniques

Targets, substrates and logbooks are separate entries because each one has its own life:

  • A target is used in many runs. Storing it once means its material, manufacturer and purchase date are entered once, and every run that used it can be found from the target.
  • A substrate (sample) outlives the run that made it: it is measured later, post-processed, or used as a recipe target. In-situ measurements and later runs refer to it.
  • A logbook is one run.

NOMAD's reference picker searches for other entries; it cannot pick a section inside the entry being edited. This is a second reason why targets and substrates are their own entries: steps can then pick them from a drop-down.

docs.title: Why substrates are created by the logbook
docs.text: The mock-up creates substrates inside the run form, and the sample user ID needs the run's system and date. So you fill in the substrate in the logbook, and on save the logbook creates a PLD Substrate entry from it (using create_archive from nomad-material-processing) and links it. The file is named after the sample user ID. If a file with that name already exists, it is linked rather than overwritten, so substrate entries are never replaced by accident.

docs.title: SA-PLD and LA-PLD
docs.text:
Both logbooks share the PLDLogbook base: system details, laser details, targets, substrates, recipe, in-situ techniques and all step logic. They differ only in:

SA-PLD LA-PLD Substrate carriers Omicron, 1" Omicron, 1", 4" wafer, sample select Particle reduction plate – in use / not in use Deposition step scan substrate stage scan yes/no + cartesian scan heater scan type: polar (default) or cartesian

Each system has its own step classes (SAPLDStep and LAPLDStep and their subclasses). When you add a step, NOMAD offers all sections that inherit from the step type of the steps sub-section. Separate step classes mean an SA-PLD logbook offers only SA-PLD steps. It also means the sputter deposition step, which belongs to the separate sputter schema, is never offered in a PLD logbook. The shared content of the steps (pre-ablation, heating, deposition, cool-down) lives in common base classes, so it is defined only once.

docs.title: Generated (read-only) fields
docs.text:
Some fields have no input box: they are filled in by the plugin on save. This is on purpose: these values are derived from other fields or from another entry, and typing them by hand would let them disagree with their source.

Field Where Why it is read-only How to change it PVD system logbook Fixed by the logbook type. A free choice would allow an "SA-PLD" logbook with LA-PLD carriers and steps. Use the other logbook type. Sample user ID substrates in the logbook, PLD Substrate Built as <system>_<date>_<run>_<sample number>, so IDs always follow the same pattern and match the data they are made of. Change the system, date, run number or sample number. Sample UUID substrates in the logbook, PLD Substrate Generated once and never changed, because it is printed on QR labels. Editing it would break the link between a label and its sample. Not changeable. Material, manufacturer, purchase date targets in the logbook Copied from the PLD Target entry, for checking your selection. Correct the PLD Target entry. Target number pre-ablation and deposition steps Copied from the target details, so the steps always show the number the target has in this run. Change it in the target details. Applied recipe load recipe A record of what was applied. Apply a recipe. Energy, intensity LA-EDS Calculated from / read from the spectrum. Change E0 or the energy per channel.

In the PLD Substrate entry itself, PVD system, run number and sample number are editable. A substrate entry can also be created by hand, without a logbook, and needs these fields for its sample user ID.

Note

The 1st window transmission is calculated but not read-only: you can override it, see below.

docs.title: Laser calibration
docs.text:
The laser energy is measured before and after the chamber, so the beam passes both windows between the two readings:

E_after = E_before × T1 × T2   →   T1 = E_after / (E_before × T2)

T2 (the 2nd window) is 92 % by default. T1 is calculated on every save unless transmission window 1 manual is ticked and a value is entered; then the typed value is kept. With a missing energy, or an energy before the chamber of 0, nothing is calculated.

Formula to be confirmed

The mock-up wrote the formula as E_after / E_before × T₂. Read literally ((E_after / E_before) × T2) that contradicts E_after = E_before × T1 × T2, so the schema uses E_after / (E_before × T2). If the literal formula is meant, change transmission_window_1() in laser.py.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
A recipe is not a separate entry type: any earlier logbook of the same system can be used as one. Applying it copies the process steps into the current logbook. Copying a snapshot, rather than linking to the recipe, means:

  • the new logbook records exactly what was done in this run, even if the recipe logbook is edited later;
  • the copied steps can be changed for this run without changing the recipe.

The recipe field keeps the link to where the steps came from.

The copy keeps references to targets, but replaces the substrate of deposition steps with the chosen substrate. This is how "do not copy the substrate identity" is implemented. References to entries in the recipe's upload are rewritten to absolute references, so they still point to the right entry when the recipe comes from another upload.

The copy is triggered by a tick box (apply_recipe) that is unticked after the copy. Saving again therefore does not copy again. See Reproduce a run with a recipe for the details.

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
Values are stored in SI units (Pa, J, m, K, ...) and shown in the units of the lab (mbar, mJ, mm, °C, ...). You type values in the shown unit in the form. In archive files (YAML/JSON) values must be given in the SI unit.

Exceptions, stored as plain numbers:

  • percentages (window transmissions, attenuator position, valve position), in %;
  • gas flows are stored in cm³/min, which is the same number as sccm.

Ramp rates are in K/min, which is the same number as °C/min. Temperatures are stored in K and shown in °C.

docs.title: In-situ techniques
docs.text:
In-situ techniques are their own section and not part of a deposition step, because a sample can be measured outside a deposition run, e.g. during post-processing of an older sample. They can be recorded in the logbook of the run or in a stand-alone PLD In-situ Techniques entry. Both have optional links to a sample and to a run.

For each technique the native file (which only the instrument software can open) and the exported file (which other programs can read) are stored separately where both exist. The LA-EDS energy axis is not stored in the .sp0 file and is rebuilt from E0 and the energy per channel. The .sp0 reader is still to be written; the LA-EDS spectrum supplier changes from RSX1000 to RaySpec RSX2000, so the reader is kept separate and easy to replace.

docs.title: The PLD logbook dashboard
docs.text: The dashboard lives in src/differ_pld4e_schemas/dashboards/pld_logbook/. It is part of this plugin, so the form and the schemas it writes are always released together.

docs.title: Why a dashboard
docs.text:
The NOMAD entry editor shows every field of a schema section and lets you save at any time. It cannot hide a field depending on another field, and it cannot refuse to save an incomplete entry. For the PLD logbooks this means users see LA-PLD fields on SA-PLD runs, polar and cartesian scan fields at the same time, and logbooks can be saved half-empty.

A dashboard plugin is a FastAPI app that NOMAD mounts under <NOMAD URL>/dashboards/<id>/, so it runs on the same origin as NOMAD and can use the NOMAD API with the user's session. The PLD logbook dashboard uses that to offer its own form with conditional fields and a completeness check, and then writes normal NOMAD entries of the PLD4Energy schemas.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
browser (static/app.js)                     dashboard app (FastAPI)
  form, live checks  ── GET  api/spec ──►     spec.py   form definition
                     ── POST api/archive ─►   rules.py  validation (again)
                     ◄─ archive files ────    convert.py form ⇄ archive (SI units)
                     ── POST api/form-from-archive (open logbook / recipe)

browser ──► NOMAD API (with the user's session)
  /users/me, /uploads, /entries/query, /entries/archive/query,
  PUT /uploads/<id>/raw/   (in-situ files, substrate and logbook archives)
  • spec.py is the single definition of the form: sections, fields, units, choices, which fields are required and when a field is shown (visible_if). The browser renders the form from it and the server validates against it.
  • rules.py evaluates conditions, computed values (1st window transmission, sample user ID) and validates a form. static/app.js contains the same rules so problems show while typing; the server always validates again before it builds anything.
  • convert.py turns a complete form into archive files, converting values from the unit of the form field to the unit of the schema quantity with pint, and reads saved logbooks back into a form.

docs.title: Completeness
docs.text:
A field is required when it is visible and marked required. Hidden fields are never required, so choosing Cartesian scan makes the cartesian fields required and the polar fields irrelevant. Lists have a minimum number of items, unique values (targets, target numbers, sample user IDs), and the steps need at least one deposition step. A ticked in-situ technique needs at least one file.

The save button stays disabled while anything is missing, and api/archive refuses to build archive files for an incomplete form, so incomplete logbooks cannot be written through the dashboard.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
1. The form is validated by the server, which also returns the file name of the logbook (<system>_<date>_<run name>.archive.json).
  2. In-situ files are uploaded to pld_files/<logbook file name>/.
  3. One PLD Substrate archive is written per new substrate, named after its sample user ID, and the logbook archive refers to it by file name. A substrate that already has an entry is not written again.
  4. The logbook is written. A new logbook never overwrites an existing file; an opened logbook is overwritten.

Each file is written with wait_for_processing=true, so NOMAD's processing errors and warnings are shown in the log.

docs.title: Conditional fields
docs.text:
Conditions are small JSON objects, evaluated in the browser and on the server:

{'key': 'heater_scan_type', 'equals': 'Polar scan'}       # same step
{'key': '/run/system', 'equals': 'LA-PLD'}                # anywhere in the form
{'all': [...]} / {'any': [...]}                           # combinations

Choices can also depend on another field (options_by), e.g. the substrate carriers depend on the PVD system.

docs.title: Develop and test
docs.text:
From the plugin folder:

uv run pytest            # all tests
uv run ruff check src tests
uv run ruff format src tests

tests/test_pld_schema.py covers the PLD schemas; tests/data/example_*_pld.archive.yaml are example entries, which are also tested.

To check an archive file with the full NOMAD processing, run from the distribution root:

uv run nomad parse packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas/tests/data/example_sa_pld.archive.yaml

docs.title: Adding or changing a section
docs.text:
1. Define the section in the module it belongs to, using ELNAnnotation components for editable fields. Store numbers in SI units, with defaultDisplayUnit for the unit shown in the form.
  2. Fields without an ELN component are read-only in the form. Use that only for values that are set in normalize, and say so in the description.
  3. New modules must be imported in schema_packages/schema_package.py.
  4. A new process step for a PLD system must inherit from SAPLDStep or LAPLDStep (plus a shared base for its content), or it will not be offered in the logbook. Do not let other steps inherit from these classes.
  5. Add tests and update the reference.

docs.title: The shared schema package
docs.text:
All modules share one m_package (from differ_pld4e_schemas/__init__.py). NOMAD renames a package to the module of the last section defined in it. The GUI stores an entry's type as <package name>.<section name> and finds it again by importing that module. schema_package.py therefore renames the package to itself after importing everything and exposes every section there. Entry types are then stored as differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.<Section>.

test_section_qualified_names_resolve checks that this keeps working. If you rename a section, entries that already use the old name no longer load.

docs.title: Save logic
docs.text:
PLDLogbook.normalize runs, in this order:

  1. date default and laser details section;
  2. target details: copy target info, check for duplicates;
  3. substrates: sample user ID, UUID, create the PLD Substrate entries;
  4. recipe: copy steps if apply_recipe is ticked;
  5. step targets: fill in a single target, copy target numbers, warn about unselected targets.

NOMAD normalizes sub-sections before their parents, so step-level logic (scan sub-sections, T1) has already run when the logbook's normalize runs.

docs.title: The PLD logbook dashboard
docs.text:
Code: src/differ_pld4e_schemas/dashboards/pld_logbook/

File Contents __init__.py Dashboard entry point app.py FastAPI app: serves the page, api/spec, api/validate, api/archive, api/form-from-archive spec.py Form definition rules.py Conditions, computed values, validation convert.py Form ⇄ archive conversion static/ Page (index.html, app.js, style.css), no build step

docs.title: Add or change a dashboard field
docs.text:
Most changes only touch spec.py:

number(
    'spot_size',               # key in the form data
    'Spot size',               # label
    'mm^2',                    # unit the user types in (pint)
    unit_label='mm²',          # how the unit is shown
    archive='laser.spot_size', # quantity path in the schema section
    visible_if={'key': '/run/system', 'equals': 'LA-PLD'},  # optional
)
  • The quantity must exist in the PLD schemas; values are converted to its unit. test_spec_archive_paths_exist_in_schema checks every step field.
  • Fields are required unless required=False (comments, booleans and computed fields are optional by default).
  • Choices that also exist in the schema are checked against it by test_spec_choices_match_schema.

If you add a new kind of rule or computed value, implement it in both rules.py and static/app.js, and add a test.

docs.title: Run the dashboard
docs.text:
• Tests: uv run pytest tests/dashboards
  • In NOMAD: restart uv run poe start and open http://localhost:8000/nomad-oasis/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-pld-logbook/. Changes to static/ only need a browser reload; Python changes need a restart.

When you change a schema quantity the form uses (rename, unit, choices), update spec.py in the same change; the dashboard tests fail until both agree.

docs.title: In a local development setup (nomad-distro-dev)
docs.text:
Development happens in nomad-distro-dev, with the plugin checked out in packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas.

  1. Make sure the root pyproject.toml of the distribution lists the plugin and its dependency nomad-material-processing:

    [project]
dependencies = [
    "differ-pld4e-schemas",
    "nomad-material-processing",
    # ...
]

[tool.uv.sources]
differ-pld4e-schemas = { workspace = true }
nomad-material-processing = { workspace = true }

  2. Install: uv sync.

  3. Start NOMAD: uv run poe start. The new entry types appear under Create from schema in an upload.

docs.title: When do changes show up?
docs.text:
You changed Do this Python code of the schemas Stop NOMAD and run uv run poe start again. pyproject.toml (dependencies, entry points) uv sync, then restart. A new package in packages/ Add it to pyproject.toml, uv sync, then restart.

Entries that were processed with an older version of the schema are not updated automatically. Save them again in the form, or reprocess the upload.

Every folder in packages/ must be a Python project

The distribution uses packages/* as a uv workspace. A folder there without a pyproject.toml makes every uv command fail with Workspace member ... is missing a pyproject.toml.

docs.title: In a NOMAD Oasis
docs.text:
Add the plugin (and nomad-material-processing) to the plugin dependencies of your Oasis distribution, e.g. as a Git dependency:

dependencies = [
    "differ-pld4e-schemas @ git+https://github.com/timval-differ/DIFFER-PLD4E-schemas.git",
]

Then rebuild and restart the Oasis. Read the NOMAD plugin documentation for the details.

The plugin registers two entry points:

Entry point What it adds differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages:schema_package_entry_point The schemas ("PLD4Energy Schemas") differ_pld4e_schemas.dashboards:pld_logbook_dashboard_entry_point The PLD logbook dashboard, at <NOMAD URL>/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-pld-logbook/

docs.title: Reproduce a run with a recipe
docs.text:
A recipe is the list of process steps of an earlier run, with all their parameters: pre-ablation, heating, deposition and cool-down steps, with gases, pressures, temperatures, laser settings and stage positions. Loading a recipe copies those steps into the logbook you are working on, so you can run the same process again on a substrate of your choice.

There is no separate "recipe" entry type: any earlier logbook of the same PLD system is a recipe. Name your logbooks clearly so you can find good recipes later.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Repeat a deposition on a fresh substrate.
  • Make a series of samples with the same process and change one parameter each time.
  • Run the same process on an existing sample again, e.g. a post-processing step.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the new logbook (SA-PLD Logbook or LA-PLD Logbook, the same type as the recipe) and fill in the system details, laser details and targets as usual.
  2. Add the substrate under substrates and save. This creates the PLD Substrate entry the recipe will be applied to. If you want to use an existing substrate instead, skip this step.
  3. Open load recipe and fill in:
    • recipe: the earlier logbook to copy from;
    • substrate (optional): the substrate to link the copied deposition steps to. If you leave it empty, the first substrate created in this logbook is used;
    • tick apply recipe.
  4. Save.

The steps of the recipe are now added to steps. Apply recipe is unticked again and applied recipe shows the name of the recipe that was used.

  1. Go through the copied steps and change whatever is different in this run (see After applying), then save again.

docs.title: What is copied
docs.text:
Part of the recipe Copied? Notes Process steps yes All steps, in order, with all their sub-sections (gases, laser, target stage, heater stage position, scans). Substrate of the deposition steps no Replaced by the substrate you chose in load recipe. The recipe's own substrate is never copied, so the new run cannot accidentally be recorded on the old sample. Target of each step yes Steps keep pointing to the same PLD Target entries as in the recipe. Target details only if empty If this logbook has no targets yet, the recipe's targets (including their target numbers) are copied. If you already selected targets, they are kept as they are. Target number in the steps recalculated Taken from this logbook's target details on save. Step name, start time, duration, comments yes Update start times and comments for the new run. Laser details (calibration) no Calibrate the laser for every run. System details (date, base pressure, carrier, particle reduction plate) no Substrates no In-situ techniques no

The copy is a snapshot. Changing the recipe logbook later does not change the logbooks it was applied to. The recipe field keeps the link to the recipe, so you can always see where the steps came from.

docs.title: After applying
docs.text:
Check after every recipe:

  • Targets. If the recipe uses a target that is not in this logbook's target details, the step gives a warning on save and its target number stays empty. Add the target under targets, or pick another target in the step.
  • Target numbers. Targets move, so check the target numbers in the target details. The steps take their target number from there.
  • Substrate. All copied deposition steps are linked to one substrate. For a logbook with several substrates, change the substrate in the steps that belong to another substrate.
  • Start times and comments are those of the recipe run.

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• Same system only. An SA-PLD recipe can only be applied to an SA-PLD logbook and an LA-PLD recipe only to an LA-PLD logbook: the step types differ. Selecting a recipe of the other system gives an error and nothing is copied. The recipe picker may also list other process entries, such as sputter depositions. Choose a PLD logbook.
  • Steps are added, not replaced. Steps already in the logbook stay and the recipe steps are added after them. Delete steps you don't need.
  • Applying twice adds the steps twice. Apply recipe is unticked after each copy, so saving again does not copy again. But if you tick it again, the steps are added a second time.
  • No recipe or no substrate. Without a recipe, ticking apply recipe gives an error. Without a substrate (none chosen and none created in this logbook), the steps are copied and their substrate stays empty. Fill it in afterwards.

docs.title: Example: a series on new substrates
docs.text:
Run 1 is the reference run, STO on Si. For run 2:

  1. Create an SA-PLD Logbook STO on Si (repeat), fill in date, base pressure, carrier and laser details.
  2. Add substrate run 2, sample 1, and save. This creates SA-PLD_<date>_2_1.
  3. Under load recipe select STO on Si, leave substrate empty, tick apply recipe and save.
  4. All steps of run 1 are now in run 2. Their deposition steps are linked to SA-PLD_<date>_2_1, and the targets of run 1 are selected. Change the target numbers if the targets moved, and change the number of pulses if this sample should be thicker.

docs.title: In an archive file
docs.text:
You can also apply a recipe from a YAML or JSON archive file. A logbook in the same upload is referenced by its file name:

data:
  m_def: differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.SAPLDLogbook
  name: STO on Si (repeat)
  load_recipe:
    recipe: '../upload/archive/mainfile/sto_on_si.archive.yaml#data'
    apply_recipe: true

docs.title: Use the PLD logbook dashboard
docs.text:
The PLD logbook dashboard is a guided form for the logbook of an SA-PLD or LA-PLD run. It saves the run as normal entries of this plugin's schemas: an SA-PLD or LA-PLD logbook, plus a PLD Substrate entry for each new substrate. Everything it saves can afterwards be viewed and edited in NOMAD as usual; see Use the PLD logbooks.

Compared with the NOMAD entry editor, the dashboard:

  • shows only the fields that apply to your choices (system, scan type, gases, in-situ techniques, ...);
  • only saves the logbook when every required field is filled in;
  • converts lab units (mbar, mJ, °C, mm, ...) to the units NOMAD stores.

docs.title: Open it
docs.text: Log in to NOMAD first. Then open PLD logbook from NOMAD's dashboards menu, or go to <NOMAD URL>/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-pld-logbook/ (locally: http://localhost:8000/nomad-oasis/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-pld-logbook/).

docs.title: Fill in a run
docs.text:
Work through the sections on the left; Next takes you to the next one. The number next to a section is the number of things still missing there, and a green tick means the section is complete. Missing fields are marked once you leave a section with Next, or straight away for fields you have edited.

  1. System details. Choose the PVD system first: it decides which carriers, scan options and fields are offered. LA-PLD also asks for the particle reduction plate.
  2. Laser details. Enter the energies before and after the chamber. The 1st window transmission is calculated as you type; switch on Enter the 1st window transmission manually to type your own value instead.
  3. Targets. Pick each target in the system and enter its target number for this run. A target that is not in the database yet can be added with New target in the database.
  4. Substrates. Create the substrates of this run (the sample user ID is shown as you type), or pick an existing substrate, e.g. for post-processing.
  5. Process steps. Add the steps in order with the + ... buttons. Each step can be moved up or down, removed, and folded away with a click on its title. The target and substrate of a step are chosen from the targets and substrates above, so they always match. At least one pulsed laser deposition step is required.
    • Tick a background gas to fill in its set flow, read-out flow, valve position and whether the valve was fixed.
    • SA-PLD: switch on Substrate stage scan for the cartesian scan fields.
    • LA-PLD: choose the heater scan type; Polar scan is the default.
  6. In-situ techniques. Tick each technique you used and add at least one of its files. Files are uploaded when you save.
  7. Review and save. Lists everything that is still missing; click an item to jump to the field. Choose an upload (or + New upload) and save.

Saving creates the PLD Substrate entries first and then the logbook, and shows NOMAD's processing messages. After saving, the form stays open: saving again updates the same logbook.

docs.title: Your draft
docs.text: The form is kept in your browser while you work, so you can close the page and continue later on the same computer. Files you chose but did not save yet are not kept: choose them again. New logbook clears the form.

docs.title: Repeat a run (recipe)
docs.text: Choose the PVD system, then Load recipe and pick an earlier logbook of the same system. Its process steps are added after your current steps; if you have not selected any targets yet, its targets are taken over too. Substrates are not copied: choose the substrate in each deposition step.

docs.title: Change a saved logbook
docs.text: Open logbook loads a saved logbook into the form. Saving overwrites it. Substrates that already have an entry are not created again. The logbook must be in an upload you can edit (not published).

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Required fields are marked with *. Comments are optional.
  • The dashboard checks the form again on the server before anything is saved.
  • A new logbook never overwrites an existing file: if a logbook with the same system, date and run name, or a substrate with the same sample user ID, already exists in the upload, saving stops with a message.

docs.title: Use the PLD logbooks
docs.text:
Short guides for the everyday tasks. For a complete walk-through of a run, see the tutorial. For every field and unit, see the reference.

Save to update

Calculated and copied values (sample IDs, 1st window transmission, target numbers, copied recipe steps, ...) are updated when the entry is saved, and the checks run at the same time. Messages appear after saving.

docs.title: Manage the target database
docs.text:
Every physical target is one PLD Target entry.

  • Add a target: create a PLD Target entry with material, manufacturer and purchase date (optionally diameter, thickness, purity).
  • Naming: the entry is named after the name field, or after the material if the name is empty. Do not put the target number in the name: target positions change, and the number is entered per run in the logbook.
  • Two targets of the same material: give them different names, e.g. Fe2O3 (Praxair 2024) and Fe2O3 (Pi-Kem 2025), so you can tell them apart in the drop-down.

docs.title: Start a logbook
docs.text:
Create an SA-PLD Logbook or LA-PLD Logbook. Pick the logbook of the system you ran on: it decides which carriers, step types and scan options are offered, and the PVD system field is set by it.

Fill in name, date (defaults to the first save), base pressure (mbar) and substrate carrier. For LA-PLD, also set particle reduction plate.

docs.title: Record the laser calibration
docs.text:
Open laser details and enter the energy before and after the chamber (mJ). Transmission of the 2nd window is pre-filled with 92 %.

On save, the 1st window transmission is calculated as T1 = E_after / (E_before × T2):

You did Result on save Entered both energies T1 is calculated (and recalculated on every save). Typed your own T1, manual not ticked Your value is replaced by the calculated one. Typed your own T1 and ticked manual Your value is kept. Ticked manual but left T1 empty T1 is calculated. Energy before chamber is 0 or an energy is missing T1 is not calculated (a warning is given for 0).

docs.title: Select the targets of a run
docs.text:
Add one targets entry per target in the system: pick the PLD Target and enter its target number for this run. Material, manufacturer and purchase date are copied in on save so you can check your choice.

Checks: selecting the same target twice is an error; using a target number twice is a warning.

docs.title: Create substrates
docs.text:
Add one substrates entry per substrate, with sample name, run number, sample number, size, material and comments, and save. Then:

  • sample user ID becomes <system>_<date>_<run>_<sample number> (date as YYYY-MM-DD, from the logbook date). It is only filled in once system, date, run number and sample number are all known.
  • sample UUID is generated once and never changes.
  • a PLD Substrate entry is created in the same upload (file <sample user ID>.archive.json) and linked in substrate.

Two substrates with the same sample user ID give a warning.

The substrate entry is created once

After the PLD Substrate entry exists, changes to the substrate in the logbook are not copied to it. Correct the PLD Substrate entry itself. Clearing the substrate field and saving links the existing entry again (found by its file name) without changing it. To have it created anew from the logbook, delete the PLD Substrate entry first, then clear the field and save.

To use a substrate that already exists, e.g. from an earlier run, skip substrates and pick the PLD Substrate directly in the deposition step (or in load recipe).

docs.title: Add process steps
docs.text: Add steps under steps in the order they were done. Only the steps of the logbook's own system are offered: pre-ablation, heating, pulsed laser deposition and cool-down. There is deliberately no sputter step in the PLD logbooks. Add a step type as often as you need; for a multilayer just add another deposition step.

docs.title: Background gases (every step)
docs.text:
Add one background gases entry per gas that was on:

Field Meaning gas Ar, O2 or N2 set flow flow set on the controller (sccm) read-out flow flow measured / read out (sccm) valve position valve position on the controller (%) valve position fixed ticked if the valve was kept at a fixed position

docs.title: Target of a pre-ablation or deposition step
docs.text: Pick the target in target. The target number is taken from the target details on save, so the step always shows the current number. If only one target is selected in the logbook, empty step targets are filled in automatically. A step target that is not selected in the target details gives a warning.

docs.title: Laser settings
docs.text: The laser sub-section of pre-ablation and deposition steps holds laser mode, laser voltage (kV), magnification, mask size, spot size (mm²), fluence (J/cm²), energy (mJ), attenuator position (%), frequency (Hz) and number of pulses.

docs.title: Heater stage
docs.text:
Deposition steps have a heater stage position with x, y, z (mm), tilt and spin (degrees).

  • SA-PLD: tick substrate stage scan if the stage scanned. On save a cartesian scan sub-section is added for x/y offset (mm), scan rate (mm/s) and rotation rate (rpm). Scan values while the box is unticked give a warning.

  • LA-PLD: choose heater scan type: Polar scan (default) or Cartesian scan. On save the matching sub-section is added:

    Polar scan Unit radius start mm radius stop mm pulse spacing mm max laser frequency Hz number of scans –

    Values in the scan type that is not selected are ignored, with a warning.

docs.title: Target stage
docs.text: Pre-ablation and deposition steps have a target stage sub-section: start x/y position, x/y offset and scan area (mm).

docs.title: Reproduce a run
docs.text: See Reproduce a run with a recipe.

docs.title: Record in-situ measurements
docs.text:
In-situ techniques are a separate part of the logbook (in situ techniques), not part of a step. For measurements that do not belong to a new run, e.g. an older sample that is post-processed, create a stand-alone PLD In-situ Techniques entry. Its sample (a PLD Substrate) and process (a logbook) fields are optional.

Add one sub-section per technique (more than one per technique is allowed, e.g. one RHEED entry per capture):

Technique Software Fields RHEED KSA 400 pattern capture: native .img and exported .png; ROI intensity map: native .kdt and exported .txt MIC EZ-Curve native .ezc and exported .csv LA-EDS RSX1000 (later RaySpec RSX2000) .sp0 file, energy offset E0 (eV), energy per channel (eV), number of channels SE, OES, SHG – one data file each

Native files can only be reopened in the instrument software. Upload them anyway: they are the raw data. The exported files can be opened elsewhere.

docs.title: LA-EDS spectrum
docs.text:
The .sp0 file has no energy axis; it is rebuilt as E = E0 + channel number × energy per channel (channels counted from 0) and plotted as intensity versus energy.

Not yet automatic

The .sp0 file is not read yet: the location of E0 in the file still has to be confirmed with an example file. Until then the spectrum (intensity per channel) can only be added via an archive file, together with E0 and the energy per channel.

docs.title: Write logbooks as archive files
docs.text:
Instead of using the form, you can upload YAML or JSON archive files; see tests/data/example_sa_pld.archive.yaml and tests/data/example_la_pld.archive.yaml.

  • Use m_def: differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.SAPLDLogbook (or LAPLDLogbook, PLDTarget, PLDSubstrate, InSituTechniquesEntry). Steps need their own m_def, e.g. ...schema_package.SAPLDDepositionStep.
  • Numbers are in SI units in archive files, whatever the form shows: Pa (not mbar), J (not mJ), m (not mm), K (not °C), m² for spot size, J/m² for fluence. For example 1e-8 mbar is 1.0e-6, 500 mJ is 0.5 and 700 °C is 973.15.
  • Reference an entry in the same upload by file name: '../upload/archive/mainfile/<file name>#data'.

docs.title: Messages after saving
docs.text: Message Level What to do Target ... is selected more than once. error Remove the duplicate target. Target number ... is used twice. warning Correct the target numbers. Substrate ... is defined twice. warning Two substrates share run and sample number; correct one. Step ... uses a target that is not selected in the target details. warning Add the target to the target details or change the step. Laser energy before chamber is 0, cannot compute T1. warning Correct the energy. Scan parameters are given but substrate stage scan is off. warning Tick the scan or remove the scan values (SA-PLD). Cartesian/Polar scan parameters are ignored for a ... scan. warning Check the heater scan type (LA-PLD). Select a recipe before applying it. error Pick a recipe in load recipe. The recipe is from ..., not from .... error Use a recipe of the same system. LA-EDS number of channels does not match the intensity. warning Check the number of channels.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
All sections of the PLD schemas with their fields. Unit is the unit shown in the form; archive files take the SI unit (see Explanation › Units). Fields marked generated are filled in on save and cannot be edited (see Explanation › Generated fields).

The m_def to use in archive files is differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.<Section>, e.g. differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.SAPLDLogbook.

docs.title: Tutorial: your first SA-PLD run
docs.text:
This tutorial walks through recording one complete SA-PLD run: SrTiO3 deposited on a Si substrate. You will:

  1. add the target to the target database,
  2. create the logbook and fill in the system and laser details,
  3. select the target and create the substrate,
  4. add the process steps,
  5. attach in-situ data.

The LA-PLD logbook works the same way; the differences are listed at the end.

Saving

Many fields are filled in or checked when you save the entry: the sample ID, the 1st window transmission, the target number in each step, and so on. If a value you expect is missing, save first.

docs.title: 1. Add the target to the target database
docs.text:
Targets are stored once, as their own PLD Target entries, and reused by every run.

  1. In your upload, create a new entry of type PLD Target.
  2. Fill in material (SrTiO3), manufacturer (Pi-Kem) and purchase date. Optionally add diameter, thickness and purity.
  3. Save. The entry is named after the material (SrTiO3). You can set a different name if you have two targets of the same material, e.g. SrTiO3 (Pi-Kem 2024).

Tip

The target number is not part of the target entry. Targets are moved in and out of the system, so the number is entered per run in the logbook.

If the target already exists, skip this step.

docs.title: 2. Create the logbook
docs.text:
1. Create a new entry of type SA-PLD Logbook.
  2. Fill in the run details:
    • name: a short name for the run, e.g. STO on Si;
    • datetime: the run date. If you leave it empty it is set to the moment you first save;
    • base pressure (mbar);
    • substrate carrier: Omicron carrier or 1" carrier.

PVD system is already set to SA-PLD and cannot be changed: it is fixed by the logbook type (see Explanation).

docs.title: Laser details
docs.text:
Do the laser calibration as described in the section description: attenuator 100% open, 1 Hz, HV NGR mode with HV = 22 kV, 500 mJ, mask 5x18 mm. Then open laser details and enter:

  • energy before chamber and energy after chamber (mJ);
  • transmission window 2: pre-filled with 92 %, change it if needed.

Save. Transmission window 1 is calculated for you as T1 = E_after / (E_before × T2). To enter your own value instead, tick transmission window 1 manual, type the value and save.

docs.title: 3. Select the target and create the substrate
Targets
docs.text:
Add one targets sub-section per target loaded in the system:

  • target: pick SrTiO3 from the target database;
  • target number: the position number of the target in the system today.

Save. Material, manufacturer and purchase date are copied from the target entry so you can check you picked the right one. Selecting the same target twice is reported as an error; using the same target number twice gives a warning.

docs.title: Substrates
docs.text:
Add one substrates sub-section per substrate:

  • sample name: e.g. Si_STO-20nm (suggested format Substrate_ThinFilm-thickness_next_layer);
  • run number and sample number;
  • size, substrate material and comments.

Save. The plugin then:

  • fills in sample user ID as SA-PLD_<date>_<run>_<sample number>, e.g. SA-PLD_2026-10-22_1_1;
  • generates a sample UUID (use it for a QR label);
  • creates a PLD Substrate entry for the substrate in the same upload and links it in substrate.

That PLD Substrate entry is the sample's identity from now on: deposition steps, recipes and later in-situ measurements refer to it.

docs.title: 4. Add the process steps
docs.text:
Add sub-sections to steps in the order you ran them. The logbook only offers SA-PLD steps: Pre-ablation step, Heating step, Pulsed laser deposition step and Cool-down step. You can add each type as often as you need, e.g. deposition, heating, deposition for a multilayer.

Every step has:

  • pressure (mbar) during the step;
  • background gases: add one entry per gas, with the gas (Ar, O2 or N2), the set flow and read-out flow (sccm), the valve position and whether the valve position was fixed;
  • description for comments.

docs.title: Pre-ablation step
docs.text:
• target: one of the targets from step 3. If only one target is selected, it is filled in on save. The target number is copied from the target details.
  • substrate temperature (°C);
  • target stage: start x/y position, x/y offset, scan area (mm);
  • laser: laser mode, laser voltage (kV), magnification, mask size, spot size (mm²), fluence (J/cm²), energy (mJ), attenuator position (%), frequency (Hz) and number of pulses.

docs.title: Heating and cool-down steps
docs.text: Ramp rate (K/min, which is the same number as °C/min) and temperature setpoint (°C), plus pressure and gases.

docs.title: Pulsed laser deposition step
docs.text:
Everything from the pre-ablation step, plus:

  • substrate: the PLD Substrate created in step 3;
  • heater stage position: x, y, z (mm), tilt and spin (degrees);
  • substrate stage scan: tick it if the substrate stage scanned. On save a cartesian scan sub-section is added for the x/y offset (mm), scan rate (mm/s) and rotation rate (rpm).

Save. Check the messages after saving: a warning tells you, for example, that a step uses a target that is not in the target details.

docs.title: 5. Attach in-situ data
docs.text: Open in situ techniques in the logbook and add a sub-section for each technique you used: RHEED, MIC, SE, LA-EDS, OES or SHG. Upload the files into the matching fields, e.g. for RHEED the native .img capture and the exported .png. See Use the PLD logbooks for the details per technique.

docs.title: Differences for an LA-PLD run
docs.text:
Use an LA-PLD Logbook instead. Everything above applies, plus:

  • the substrate carrier also offers 4" wafer carrier and Sample select carrier;
  • particle reduction plate: in use or not in use;
  • the deposition step has a heater scan type, Polar scan (default) or Cartesian scan. On save the matching sub-section is added:
    • polar scan: radius start, radius stop, pulse spacing (mm), max laser frequency (Hz) and number of scans;
    • cartesian scan: x/y offset, scan rate and rotation rate.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Repeat this run on a new substrate: Reproduce a run with a recipe.
  • Look at complete example entries: tests/data/example_sa_pld.archive.yaml and tests/data/example_la_pld.archive.yaml in the plugin repository.
